name: Lash
description:
A cord swung and its tip cracking. This was one unfiltered sawtooth thrown upward from `$swarm`: every harmonic to Nyquist, which is a buzz, and a buzz is a synth and not a lash. A real one is two events — the cord moving air as it comes round, and the tip snapping at the end of it — and neither of them buzzes.

`swing` is the cord coming round: noise under a lowpass that opens from `$shell` to `$grit` as the cord speeds up and swells into the crack, so the lash is heard arriving. Lowpassed, not bandpassed, and only fifty milliseconds of it, because a long bright band of noise is the hiss every weapon in the set was accused of. `crack` is the tip, and it is struck rather than sprayed: a sine snapped down from `$gust` to `$grit.down` in twenty milliseconds, over `tick`, four milliseconds of noise for the edge. `cord` is a low sine under the crack, the weight of the thing being swung, short enough to be felt rather than heard as a note.

The Lash, the Cowboy and every thicket fire this, so it ships three takes.
